headline: Odyssey, an AI research company, says its new Odyssey-3 model can help control robots, humanoids, vehicles and drones.
score_reason: New on 8 Oct; broad claims with no outside evidence yet.
importance_line: If one model can steer many kinds of machines, new robots could learn tasks with less training, which would matter to robot makers and their customers; the claims are Odyssey's own and no independent test or performance figures are reported.
summary: Robotics & Automation News reports, from the company's announcement, that Odyssey-3 is a "world model", an AI trained on large numbers of examples of how the world changes so it can predict what happens next, and that Odyssey says it has controlled robots, driven vehicles, piloted drones and played video games. The firm Flexion, which works on humanoid autonomy, is among the first adopters, but the announcement gives no test results.
notes: Company announcement relayed by the trade outlet; the same story appears as C01-04.
